description: Kimchi Pancakes, or Kimchijeon, are savory, spicy, and utterly delicious Korean appetizers. Made with fermented kimchi, a crispy batter, and often other vegetables or meat, they offer a delightful texture and a burst of umami flavor. This popular dish is perfect as a snack, an appetizer, or a side dish for any Korean meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Kimchi
instructions.text: Finely chop the kimchi into small pieces. If your kimchi is very sour, you can rinse it lightly, but well-fermented sour kimchi adds great flavor. Reserve 1/4 cup of the kimchi juice.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour (if using), and sugar. Gradually add the cold water and kimchi juice, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are fine; do not overmix. Stir in the egg.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the chopped kimchi, sliced onion, and chopped green onions to the batter. Mix gently until all ingredients are evenly distributed. The batter should be thick enough to coat the ingredients but still pourable.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the entire bottom of the pan.

instructions.title: Cook the Pancakes
instructions.text: Pour about 1/2 cup of the batter into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Add more oil as needed between pancakes. Press down lightly with a spatula to ensure even cooking and crispiness.

instructions.title: Make the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: While the pancakes are cooking, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds in a small bowl. Mix well.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Remove the cooked Kimchi Pancakes from the pan and place them on a cutting board. Slice into wedges and serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Enjoy the crispy texture and spicy, savory flavor.

tips: For extra crispiness, use a combination of all-purpose flour and rice flour. The rice flour creates a lighter, crunchier texture.
Do not overmix your batter. Overmixing develops gluten, which can make your pancakes tough. A few small lumps are perfectly fine.
Serve Kimchi Pancakes immediately after cooking to enjoy their best crispy texture. They pair wonderfully with a simple soy-vinegar dipping sauce.
